title: the ring
hook: a small gold ring with a name on it, given to the one searcher Rama trusted most, crosses an ocean in a monkey's keeping

segments.voice: Yesterday: Sita found, and your line, no dreams without sleep. Rama, described detail by detail, until her joy was only half fear.

Back in Kishkindha, the monkey armies set off in four directions, search party after search party. Rama gave only one of them a token for Sita: his own ring, engraved with his name. He gave it to Hanuman. Valmiki says Rama could see that the monkey king trusted Hanuman above all, and that Hanuman would be the one to succeed. Everyone else went searching. Hanuman went searching with a ring in his keeping.
screen: `FOUR ARMIES, FOUR DIRECTIONS.` → `ONE RING, ONE SEARCHER.`

segments.voice: Now, under the shimshapa tree, Hanuman brings it out. I am a monkey, he says, the messenger of wise Rama. Look, my lady: this ring, marked with Rama's name. I've brought it so you'll believe me. Sita takes the ring in her hands, and Valmiki says she is as happy as if she had met her husband himself. Her face shines the way the moon shines when it slips free of an eclipse. Think what that ring has been through. It left Rama's hand in Kishkindha. It traveled south through forests, through the dark cave of Svayamprabha, past the despair on the beach and Sampati's news. It crossed a hundred yojanas of sea, past Mainaka, past Surasa's mouth, through Simhika, over Lanka's wall, through the palace, up a tree. And it arrived. Words can be faked. A messenger could be one of Ravana's tricks. But this is Rama's own ring, the one she knew on his hand. It says Rama is real, that he's looking, that he sent someone. It says, I haven't forgotten you, in a way no speech could. And notice Rama's choice. Out of everyone, he gave the ring to the one he trusted to get there. Some tokens are only as good as the hands they're given to.
screen: `MARKED WITH RAMA'S NAME.` · `AS IF SHE'D MET HIM HIMSELF.` · `WHAT THE RING HAS BEEN THROUGH.` · then, large: `I HAVEN'T FORGOTTEN YOU.`

segments.voice: If you're wearing a ring, a bracelet or a watch, or have any small object someone gave you, rest your attention on it; if not, think of one you remember. Feel its weight, breathe in, and think of the person it connects you to. Breathe out, and let it carry them close for a moment, no words needed.
The ring. Rama's own ring, marked with his name, carried across the sea by Hanuman, which makes Sita as happy as if she'd met Rama himself.
Your line: I haven't forgotten you. Tomorrow, what she asks next. Day six hundred twenty, done.

howItsDone: Hanuman presenting Rama's ring to Sita is a familiar scene in Ramayana painting and sculpture, and in some devotional images Hanuman kneels before Sita holding the ring up to her.

chat.meaning: Words can be faked, but Rama's own ring, marked with his name, told Sita he was real, looking, and hadn't forgotten her.

shimshapa.meaning: the tree Sita sits beneath in the grove

Svayamprabha.meaning: an ascetic who keeps a hidden city in a cave

Sampati.meaning: an old wingless vulture, Jatayu's brother

Mainaka.meaning: a mountain that rose from the sea to offer Hanuman rest

Surasa.meaning: mother of serpents, sent by the gods to test Hanuman
